visual.general_description: Four line graphs (A to D) of post-transplant liver function tests over 0 to 100 hours for three patients keyed by marker shape.
visual.detailed_description: A 2 by 2 grid of black-and-white line graphs on a white background with bold panel letters A to D, each with an x axis labeled Hours (ticks 0 to 100) and a y axis in IU/L (A, B), mg/dL (C) or unlabeled (D). A single legend to the right of panel D keys circles to Patient 1, squares to Patient 2 and triangles to Patient 3. All series decline overall after early values; in panel C the triangle series rises to an early peak before falling.

panels.general_description: Line graph of alanine transaminase over hours for three patients.
panels.detailed_description: Bold letter A at upper left. Y axis labeled IU/L with ticks 0, 500, 1000, 1500, 2000 and 2500; x axis labeled Hours with ticks 0, 25, 50, 75 and 100. Three marker-and-line series with about eight markers each at roughly 0, 6, 12, 18, 24, 48, 72 and 96 hours: circles keyed Patient 1, squares keyed Patient 2, triangles keyed Patient 3. The triangle series is highest, starting near 2000 and falling steadily to roughly 450 at the last marker. The circle series starts near 850, rises slightly near the second marker, dips, and ends near 430. The square series is lowest, starting near 450 and falling to under 100.

assignments.subject: patient

evidence.quote:
Figure 1
Liver function tests post-transplantation. A: Alanine transaminase; B: Aspartate transaminase; C: Total bilirubin; D: International ratio.
Transaminases began decreasing within the first 24 hours after transplant and the patient had normal bilirubin and INR by post-operative day 4 (Figure 1).
Transaminases decreased consistently starting 12 hours after transplant with normalization of Total-Bilirubin and INR 72 hours after transplantation (Figure 1).
Transaminases peaked in the 2000s within the first 24 hours and subsequently decreased (Figure 1A and B).

assignments.rationale: The caption names the test; the three case paragraphs each cite Figure 1 for that patient and the printed legend plots Patient 1, 2 and 3, read as roster order p1 to p3. Series are distinguished by marker shape only.

visual.general_description: Color operative photograph of a pale tan liver in a clear plastic bag containing red-pink fluid with a clear cannula attached by ties to a vessel.
visual.detailed_description: Operative photograph, portrait orientation. A gloved hand at the top holds a long translucent tube vertically; its lower end is tied with sutures to a short vessel stump on a pale tan-orange liver that lies in a clear plastic bag set in a white basin filled with red-pink fluid. A second gloved hand in a blue sleeve rests on the right lobe of the liver. A metal hemostat or clamp lies across the liver and bag, and a second short translucent tube or cuff lies at the lower left of the liver. Black suture material is visible near the cannulated vessel and at the left of the liver. Surgical drapes with blue and white fields, instruments and tubing are visible around the basin. The face and body of any person are not visible. No panel letters, arrows, text labels or scale are visible; faint printing on the upper-left glove cuff is illegible.
